transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-29
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Lena Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Sarah Ortiz (HealthTech - Security Lead), Raj Mehta (HealthTech - CTO), Emily Zhao (HealthTech - Platform)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time for this security deep dive. i'm lena from redwood, this is marcus our se.
[00:12] Sarah: hey lena, thanks, yeah we wanted to go through SSO and provisioning, plus a quick sanity check on encryption and audit logs, hey marcus.
[00:22] Marcus: hi all, yeah i'll try to keep this practical, we can share docs and a sample rbac matrix after. quick note, i'll probably say kv cache a lot which, you know, is unrelated but part of our runtime, sorry.
[00:34] Raj: that's fine. our timeline is tight so the faster we validate sso + scim the better.

[02:00] Lena: quick agenda — 1) architecture overview of SSO/SAML flow for hosted and private deployments, 2) scim provisioning patterns and attributes, 3) rbac/least privilege model + roles, 4) audit logs / retention and encryption / kms; leave time for q's and next steps. ok?
[02:18] Sarah: yup perfect.

[04:05] Marcus: so for SAML our platform supports IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. for hosted api customers we provide metadata to import into your idp, and for private/VPC deployments we can either exchange metadata directly or you can host the auth gateway in your vpc.
[04:30] Marcus: common gotcha is clock skew and cert rotations, we've got automated cert rotation for the SP if you're on hosted, and for private we give instructions to rotate on a schedule.
[04:45] Emily: for scim — do you support incremental provisioning and group sync? we don't want a full push every time.
[04:55] Marcus: yep we support PATCH and bulk operations; group-to-role mappings are how we recommend doing least-privilege, so you map idp groups to redwood roles and then those roles to permissions.

[06:20] Sarah: can you describe the role model? we try to enforce least-privilege — developers should not be able to change billing or access production logs.
[06:35] Marcus: absolutely — our common roles are admin, security/audit, platform, devops, and read-only. admin can manage account-wide settings incl. billing. platform/devops can manage deployments and keys but not billing. security/audit has access to logs and runbooks but cannot change runtime configs, and read-only is view only.
[07:05] Marcus: we typically recommend scoping admin to 1-2 people and using groups for temporary escalations. we also support session timeouts and optional MFA enforcement via your idp.

[08:40] Raj: about keys — do you integrate with our KMS? we need BYOK, hsm capable for some PHI workloads.
[08:50] Marcus: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS for hosted customers, and for dedicated/private we support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys. when using BYOK, the envelope keys remain under your control and we never persist raw key material.
[09:10] Sarah: is there an audit trail for key usage? we need to show who requested decrypt operations.
[09:18] Marcus: key usage is logged — we write an audit event when the key is used for crypto ops and that goes to our audit log stream which you can push to your SIEM via pub/sub or S3 export. retention windows are configurable depending on your plan.

[11:00] Lena: quick interjection — i'll drop the SOC2 report and encryption whitepaper after this call, and the link to our security FAQ.
[11:08] Sarah: great.

[12:30] Emily: audit logs — what are the fields in the logs? we need timestamped actor, action, resource, request id, and IP. also need immutability for compliance.
[12:45] Marcus: our logs include timestamp, user id, role, action (api call), resource id, request id, response code, and originating ip. we can forward immutable logs to a customer-controlled S3 bucket with object lock enabled for WORM-style retention.
[13:10] Sarah: ok that's useful, can you forward directly to our Splunk as well?
[13:18] Marcus: yes we have integrations for Splunk/Datadog/ELK via streaming and also kafka/pubsub connectors.

[15:00] Raj: on data residency — our data has to stay in eu-west-1 for certain customers. does redwood support regional tenancy?
[15:12] Marcus: yes — we can pin data and inference to region. hosted customers can select region on account creation; for dedicated/private we deploy in the region you choose and ensure storage and processing stay in that region.
[15:35] Sarah: any caveats for cross-region backups?
[15:40] Marcus: cross-region backups are off by default for customers who require strict residency; you can opt-in if you want cross-region replication.

[18:00] Lena: ok let's go back to SAML/SCIM specifics — sarah, emily, are you planning to use an IdP like Okta/AzureAD?
[18:12] Sarah: Okta today, likely will standardize on that.
[18:20] Marcus: great, we have an Okta quickstart and we support SAML assertions with nameID and email, and SCIM attributes including userName, displayName, emails, groups, and custom attributes. we recommend sending groups for role mapping and a custom attribute for tenant_id if you use multi-tenant separation.
[19:00] Emily: for SCIM provisioning what about deprovisioning — do you do soft-delete or immediate lockout? we need to ensure terminated users lose access instantly.
[19:12] Marcus: our SCIM implementation supports immediate deactivation; we recommend IdP-initiated deprovisioning that sets active=false. when an account is deactivated the session is invalidated and tokens are revoked.

[21:00] Sarah: are there any limitations on SCIM rate limits during bulk sync? we have 15k users.
[21:12] Marcus: for large directories we advise a staged sync; our scim endpoints support bulk but with throttles — for 15k we usually run an initial bulk import via SFTP CSV ingest and then enable SCIM incremental sync for changes.

[24:30] Raj: can you show how role mapping looks? a quick example?
[24:40] Marcus: sure — example: Okta group "hts-platform" -> redwood role "platform". Permissions enumerated: deploy:create, deploy:update, keys:read (not keys:write), logs:read. admin group -> billing:read/write, account:settings. security-audit group -> logs:read, exports:create, but not deploy:write. i'll attach a sample matrix.

[27:00] Emily: on RBAC enforcement — is it enforced at the API gateway layer or inside each service? we need strong separation.
[27:12] Marcus: enforced at the gateway and enforced at service-level; token includes scoped claims and services validate scopes. we also have an internal sync to ensure policy updates propagate within seconds.

[29:30] Sarah: how do you handle emergency access / break glass? we need an auditable process.
[29:40] Marcus: we support temporary elevated sessions with approval workflow. break glass events are logged with approver id and TTL. we can integrate with your approval tool or use our built-in workflow. everything is auditable.

[33:00] Lena: circling back — encryption in transit and at rest?
[33:10] Marcus: TLS 1.2+ in transit; at rest data encrypted with AES-256 via KMS-managed keys. metadata and logs are encrypted. for BYOK we do envelope encryption with your KMS; keys are never stored in plaintext on disk.
[33:40] Sarah: do you support customer-supplied HSM?
[33:46] Marcus: yes for private/on-prem we can wire to your HSM. for hosted we support AWS CloudHSM integrations via KMS.

[36:00] Raj: regarding compliance artifacts — SOC 2 and ISO, are you current?
[36:08] Lena: we are SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO 27001; i'll send the latest attestation and summary.
[36:18] Sarah: thanks, we'll need the SOC 2 and pen test report for procurement.

[38:30] Emily: one more thing about logging — request-level logs for model prompts: we need controls to redact pii before storing. is that configurable?
[38:45] Marcus: yes — we support configurable redaction rules and can do client-side redaction via SDKs, plus server-side redaction patterns. for sensitive workloads you can also disable prompt dump and only log metadata.

[41:00] Sarah: what about retention? we need 7 years for certain audit trails, others 90 days. can retention be different per log type?
[41:12] Marcus: retention is configurable per log type and per export. we support long-term archiving to your bucket with lifecycle rules.

[44:00] Raj: ok great. circling on next steps and POC: we want to run an SSO+SCIM test with a small set of users and validate RBAC rules and audit exports. can you host a pilot in eu-west-1?
[44:15] Marcus: yes, we can provision a dedicated pilot account in eu-west-1 and enable SCIM and SAML for testing. usually a 2-week pilot for SSO flows and RBAC mapping is enough.

[46:00] Lena: action items — i'll drop SOC2 and encryption whitepaper; marcus will attach rbac matrix and okta quickstart; emily please share idp metadata and scim attributes.
[46:20] Emily: will do, i'll send metadata by COB Tuesday.

[48:30] Sarah: any pricing impacts for dedicated pilot?
[48:40] Lena: pilot is free for 2 weeks, post-pilot we'll present dedicated pricing.

[50:00] Raj: one last question — do you have SAML cert rotation automation for long-lived service accounts?
[50:10] Marcus: we support auto-rotate for the SP cert and can provide a webhook notification for upcoming rotations. for long-lived service accounts we recommend short-lived tokens and automatic rotation.

[52:00] Lena: awesome — thanks everyone. i'll recap next steps in email.
[52:08] Sarah: thanks all.
[52:12] Raj: thanks.
[52:15] Marcus: thanks folks.

Recap / Next steps (verbal recap recorded):
- Redwood to send SOC2 Type II report, encryption whitepaper, and security FAQ (Lena).
- Redwood SE to provide RBAC matrix, Okta quickstart, and sample SCIM mappings (Marcus).
- HealthTech (Emily) to send IdP SAML metadata and SCIM attribute mapping (Emily).
- Schedule pilot in eu-west-1 for SAML+SCIM+RBAC test (target week of 2025-11-10).

Links referenced during call:  
- SOC2 attestation (will be shared)  
- Okta quickstart: https://redwood.example.com/docs/okta-quickstart  
- RBAC sample matrix (attached post-call)  
- Security FAQ: https://redwood.example.com/security-faq

End of transcript.
